candidates.title: VIVIFoCAL S1 Glasses Use Sliding Lenses to Adjust Focus as You Work
candidates.full_text:
Working at a desk rarely means looking at just one thing. A screen sits ahead, a notebook lies below, and whatever you’re making ends up somewhere between them. The VIVIFoCAL S1 adaptive eyewear is designed to adjust focus as those distances change, taking some of the fuss out of switching between tasks. The interesting part is that its lenses actually move.

That becomes particularly relevant with presbyopia, the age-related reduction in the eye’s ability to focus up close. Reading glasses help with nearby details, while multifocal lenses accommodate several distances through different viewing areas. Depending on your setup, that can mean swapping pairs or finding the right spot in a lens. It’s a small adjustment that can become a familiar part of the day. You may have grown used to adjusting to your glasses, without noticing how those small compromises shape your daily life and interrupt your work. VIVIFoCAL S1 offers a new approach: glasses should adapt to you, rather than requiring you to adapt to them.

Consider a model-building project spread across the table. The instruction sheet, the tiny piece between your fingers, and the reference on your monitor all belong to the same job. They don’t share the same viewing distance, though. The VIVIFoCAL S1’s approach is to change the optical setting as you move between them, rather than make changing glasses another step in the assembly process.

A time-of-flight sensor built into the bridge measures distance using reflected light. A controller then calculates how far the optical elements need to shift, and a miniature motor handles the movement. It’s a physical response to what’s in front of the glasses, with a specified adjustment time below 0.1 seconds.

Those moving elements form an Alvarez lens system, which changes optical power by sliding two specially shaped lenses relative to each other. The mechanism gives autofocus a surprisingly literal meaning here. Instead of asking your eyes to work with a fixed near setting, the glasses alter the optics themselves. That’s an appealing piece of design for activities that don’t stay at arm’s length.

For activities that require a consistent viewing distance, S1 also offers a Focus Lock feature. Wearers can choose between automatic focusing and a locked focus setting depending on the task. Automatic mode is suited to activities involving frequent distance changes, while Focus Lock allows users to maintain a selected focus setting during reading, detailed hands-on work, or other tasks performed at relatively fixed distances.

That also changes the relationship between your gaze and the lens. Typical progressive lenses distribute different powers across designated regions, while the VIVIFoCAL S1 is designed for a wider usable area at its selected focus. A slight head adjustment can still help the sensors identify the intended target, but the aim is less dependent on finding a particular viewing zone.

Of course, automatically adjusting focus doesn’t make your prescription irrelevant. The VIVIFoCAL S1 is made with lenses customized to your prescription, while adaptive focus handles changes in viewing distance. For wearers who also have nearsightedness, farsightedness, or astigmatism, S1 can be configured with customized prescription lenses to address their individual vision needs.

Before shipping, VIVIFoCAL will collect the latest prescription details and pupillary distance (PD) measurements from users who require prescription customization. The lenses will then be produced according to their individual specifications. Wearers can choose the included 1.59-index prescription lenses at no additional cost, or upgrade to 1.67- or 1.74-index lenses depending on their prescription and preferred lens thickness.

The companion app adds another layer of personalization, letting you fine-tune settings to suit your preferences. That makes sense for something you wear rather than merely operate. A comfortable reading distance isn’t identical for everyone, and even our own vision can fluctuate throughout the day. What feels perfectly clear in the morning may call for a slight adjustment by evening. These adjustments complement professional prescription fitting rather than replacing regular eye exams.

candidates.title: This Pocket Photo Frame Runs up to 195 Days on One Charge
candidates.full_text:
A photo frame that fits in your pocket and holds a single picture for months sounds like a gag gift. The Insta360 Toast is real, and I kind of love the idea. It’s a color E Ink photo frame, 3.7 inches across.

No screen glow at all. It sticks to a fridge, stands on a desk, or hangs from a lanyard.

Insta360 Ace Pro 2 Single Battery Bundle Price: $369.99 $399.99 (save $30.00, 8% off) Where to buy: Buy on Amazon

Insta360 Toast Price: about $64 (China launch price, converted); US price not announced 3.7-inch E Ink Spectra 6 color screen, up to 195 days per charge, 43 grams Where to buy: Insta360

Most color E Ink screens mix four inks and stop there. The Toast’s E Ink Spectra 6 panel layers six, red, yellow, blue, green, black and white, at 720 by 480 pixels. That extra color shows up in skin tones and sunsets first. Photos look warmer, deeper and less washed out than the four-color panels you get on most color E Ink gadgets today.

There’s no backlight, so the screen borrows light from the room like a sheet of paper does. It never glares back. The finish is matte, closer to a print from a photo booth than a phone display.

You read it like paper. At 234 pixels per inch, photos stay smooth up close.

Insta360 runs its own color tuning on every photo you send, which keeps faces from going flat or strange. You can see the ink dots if you press your face close. From a normal distance, it passes for a print. That visible grain is part of the charm here, not a flaw to fix.

E Ink only spends power while the picture changes, and it spends nothing at all the rest of the time. That’s over half a year. So the little 400mAh battery inside is rated for up to 195 days when you swap in a new photo once a day.

If the battery dies anyway, the last photo just stays up on the screen, right where you left it. There’s no blank white screen and no dead gadget look waiting on your shelf. Changing the picture takes patience, though, and this is where the paper act gets real. The button flips through quick previews at a tap, then the full color refresh takes about 30 seconds and flashes yellow while the ink settles into place.

Cloud space holds 200 more. You send photos from the Insta360 app over Wi-Fi or Bluetooth, and it keeps 30 on board.

Remote sending is the trick I’d actually use most, by a mile. Put a Toast on your sister’s fridge across the country, then send tonight’s dinner photo straight to it from your couch after dessert. She never has to touch a single thing on her end.

If you shoot with an Insta360 camera, the frame can pull photos straight from your Insta360+ cloud account. No exporting, no cables, no digging through your camera roll at midnight. It only takes still photos, though. Video clips and Live Photos stay on your phone, because this screen was built for one frozen moment at a time.

The Toast weighs 43 grams and measures 5.25mm thick, so it carries like a luggage tag, not a gadget. Every carry style is covered. The box includes a desk stand, a magnetic plate, a short lanyard, a leather case and a charging cable.

On the fridge it replaces the curled printout held up by a souvenir magnet. Around your neck it works like a badge, one favorite photo riding along to class, work or a convention floor.

The leather case turns it into a bag charm that clips next to your keys, your lip balm and your daily work badge. It clips on in seconds. It’s a photo you wear, which sounds silly until you picture your dog’s face on your tote.

The catch is that the Toast launched in China only, and Insta360 hasn’t announced a US price or a US date. That’s the gift play. In China it costs about $64 for one or $122 for two, converted from the yuan prices, which lands near a nice dinner out or a couple of streaming bills. A two-pack makes sense here, one for you and one for the person whose fridge you’d fill with photos every single week.

I’d skip the import hunt, because a frame that leans on an app and cloud space deserves a proper local launch. The hardware idea is sound, and the slow refresh won’t bother you once a photo is up. Pay the patience once, and it disappears into your day like a print does.

Wait for the US launch if you’re here, and watch for the Toast to land with a real US price. This one’s for the friend who prints photos and wishes every print could change with the week.

candidates.title: NOVITEC gives the Ferrari 12Cilindri a dramatic N-Largo widebody makeover
candidates.full_text:
German tuning specialist NOVITEC has spent more than two decades transforming some of the world’s most striking supercars with its distinctive widebody carbon-fiber conversions. Known as the N-Largo series, these projects aim to give already dramatic performance cars a more imposing appearance without compromising their original design character.

The transformations go beyond visual enhancements, with aerodynamic efficiency, weight, and other functional elements considered throughout the development process. Now, the German tuner has turned its attention to Ferrari’s naturally aspirated V12 grand tourer, introducing the 12Cilindri N-Largo. Developed in collaboration with German designer Vittorio Strosek, the conversion brings a wider carbon-fiber body, bespoke aerodynamic components, larger wheels and an upgraded exhaust system. Production is limited to just 20 examples worldwide, making it an object of desire.

The redesigned bodywork increases the Ferrari’s width by 7 cm at the front and 13 cm at the rear, bringing its overall width to 2,110 mm, excluding the mirrors. Rather than simply adding oversized wheel arches, the conversion incorporates extensively redesigned body panels made from lightweight, high-strength carbon fiber.

Front fascia also receives a new bumper with larger air intakes and an integrated spoiler designed to reduce front-axle lift at higher speeds. NOVITEC also removes the original Daytona-inspired black strip between the headlights, giving the front end a cleaner appearance. A redesigned carbon-fiber hood features a prominent central air outlet that exposes the V12 engine’s red intake manifolds. Additional gill-shaped openings above the front wheels help extract hot air from the wheel wells.

The changes are equally substantial at the rear. The original rear window is replaced by a body-coloured panel featuring narrow viewing slits, while a three-piece ducktail spoiler stretches across the widened rear section. The redesigned rear fascia incorporates a prominent carbon-fiber diffuser and quad exhaust outlets. NOVITEC has also reworked the aerodynamic package, replacing Ferrari’s active rear aero flaps with a fixed spoiler intended to generate additional downforce. Further openings are incorporated to improve rear brake cooling.

Filling the expanded wheel arches are bespoke NF12 N-Largo forged wheels, developed with American wheel specialist Vossen. The five-spoke Y-shaped design features a deeply concave profile, particularly at the rear. The front wheels measure 21 inches and are paired with 275/35 ZR21 tyres, while the rear gets 22-inch wheels wrapped in wider 325/30 ZR22 rubber. NOVITEC sports springs lower the ride height by approximately 30 mm, giving the car a noticeably lower stance.

The naturally aspirated 6.5-litre V12 also receives attention through an upgraded stainless-steel sports exhaust with electronically controlled butterfly valves. Drivers can adjust the exhaust character between a more restrained note and a louder soundtrack. For buyers seeking a more distinctive finish, NOVITEC offers an optional 999 fine-gold-plated exhaust system. Optional sports catalysts are also available, although the tuner has not announced a confirmed power increase for the modified engine.

12Cilindri N-Largo is available as a complete vehicle commissioned directly through NOVITEC or as a conversion for existing Ferrari owners. Interior customisation is also offered according to individual preferences. With only 20 examples planned, the project is all about bespoke detailing in a considerably more imposing interpretation of Ferrari’s V12 grand tourer.
